penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: A managed or semi-managed email hosting service requires ongoing infrastructure operations (server uptime, deliverability reputation, DNS configuration per customer) that cannot be automated by Claude alone.

penalties_applied.name: high_touch_support
penalties_applied.reason: Email deliverability issues, OTP delays, and iOS client quirks generate high-frequency, high-urgency support tickets requiring human judgment.

rationale: The segment — technical founders and indie developers self-hosting email — is identifiable but weak as a buyer: this group skews strongly toward free/self-hosted solutions and has a high DIY tolerance, meaning willingness to pay for a managed service is uncertain and likely price-sensitive. The real pain (iOS sync latency, OTP delays) is genuine and recurring, but the product required to solve it is email infrastructure — SMTP servers, IMAP daemons, deliverability management, per-domain DNS setup — which is firmly outside what the Claude factory can build or operate autonomously. Running email infrastructure for others is a high-ops, high-support product where a single outage or spam-reputation event requires immediate human intervention. The factory cannot build or operate this without Youval becoming a sysadmin for every customer. Drop.
solution_plan: This would be a managed or appliance-style email hosting service for technical users who want control without maintenance. The honest answer is that a solo non-technical operator cannot build or run this: managed email hosting requires server infrastructure, deliverability reputation management, abuse handling, and per-customer DNS configuration — none of which can be delivered via Claude prompts and a landing page. Even an affiliate or white-label arrangement around an existing provider (Fastmail, Migadu) would require technical support per customer. The segment also has a strong free-tool bias (they already self-host) that makes monetization difficult. This opportunity does not fit the autonomous factory model and should be dropped in favor of ideas where Claude can handle both building and ongoing delivery.
notes: Fails build_gates: buildability_with_ai=3 (min 6), operational_autonomy=3 (min 7), willingness_to_pay=4 (min 5). Total after penalties is 2.5 — below validate threshold. Infrastructure product requiring ongoing sysadmin work; incompatible with autonomous delivery model.
